android.desc:
Roll your sphere through each level, collecting operation cubes that multiply, add, and subtract from your running total. The order you pick them up changes everything. Get it wrong and the portal remains unreachable.

But the math is only half the challenge.

Some doors can't be opened at all. Others block the only path to the portal. Before you move, you need to figure out which doors are actually solvable — then plan the exact route to hit those numbers. Move too fast and you'll find yourself stuck with the wrong total and no way back.

Watch out for tiles that rewrite the rules mid-run. Orange tiles shift the values of every remaining cube in the level. Dark blue tiles flip your operators — your +10 becomes a −10 in an instant. Death spheres lurk throughout each level, punishing any careless move.

4 tutorial levels ease you in — 100+ levels across three difficulties, easy enough to learn in minutes, deep enough to keep you thinking for hours with no ad interruptions. Just optional ads for hints and extra lives.

If you've ever wanted a game that makes you plan like a chess player and move like an action game, this is it.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Rollquation – A Rolling-Ball Math Puzzle Game for Android (Solo Dev)

quotes.text:
Hey HN! I'm a solo dev and I just wanted to share my latest Android game — Rollquation.

The idea was to make math genuinely fun by combining it with navigation. You roll a sphere through maze-like levels, collecting numbered and operator cubes that must add up to exact values to unlock doors and reach the exit.

I also wanted the game to feel like a nice place to be, so I built it around a nature scene with trees, mountains and a waterfall. That came with a cost though, performance on older/weaker phones was an issue during my first release. I ended up building an adaptive performance system that auto-selects a quality setting (low/medium/high/ultra) based on the device's RAM. It helped a lot, though I'm still fine-tuning it.

The other big lesson was around controls. I originally used physics for the rolling sphere, which meant the ball would decelerate before changing direction which players found unresponsive and slow. Removing the physics and making movement instant transformed how the game felt.

Unity UI is not my strength and players have mentioned that it could use some work. The UI is usable but I may end up changing it.

Gameplay video: https://youtu.be/SGbQa3-ORhI

Play Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.JabGames.PathCalculationMathPuzzle

Any feedback or thoughts on the game is appreciated.
